_note: The FILM TIMELINE corpus (12-marketing-video.md Phase 1). Pins the laws a marketing film's determinism rests on: scene selection at boundaries, the contiguity/duration validation (a gap is a black hole in the advertisement), camera hold-then-move composition, single-frame tap attribution, the cut law (the INCOMING scene's cut owns the boundary, both edges), state-write sampling (sets are single-frame like taps; a tween emits its exact end value exactly once), and the exact frame count. Interpolation pins use LINEAR easing so every expected number is exact hand arithmetic; eased moves are pinned only at their endpoints, because the curve itself is already pinned by Conformance/motion and a second set of bezier expectations here would be a second opinion about it. Every expected value was derived by hand from the laws, never by the kernel under test.

sceneIndex.name: the boundary belongs to the NEXT scene (inclusive start)
one ms before the boundary is still the previous scene
the last instant belongs to the last scene

sceneAlpha.name: the first scene never fades IN (there is nothing to fade from)
a scene fades in over SCENE_FADE_MS: halfway at 160ms after entry
a scene fades out over the last 320ms: halfway at 160 before the end
the LAST scene never fades out (the encoder ends the film, not a fade)

tapAttribution._note: fps 30 means frameMs = 33.333...; the tap at scene-local 1500ms (absolute 3500ms) belongs to exactly one frame: the frame whose window [local, local+frameMs) contains 1500.

cases.name: the frame starting at local 1466.67 does not carry it
the frame starting at local 1500 carries it
the next frame does not carry it again

camera._note: Concrete moves, LINEAR ease. Home is {x:540, y:960, scale:1}. Move 1: at 200ms for 400ms to {x:300,y:500,scale:2}. Move 2: at 1000ms for 500ms back to home. Holds are exact; mid-move values are exact linear arithmetic.

cases.name: before the first move the camera is home
halfway through move 1: exact midpoint
after move 1 the camera HOLDS its target
move 2 starts FROM the held state: 40% back
after every move the camera rests where the last one ended

easedEndpoints._note: an easeInOut move is pinned only at its endpoints; the curve between them is Conformance/motion's law, not this corpus's.

validation.name: the corpus film itself is lawful
a gap between scenes refuses (and the NEXT scene now also mismatches the cursor)
scenes that end short of the declared duration refuse
a scene with no document and no words is G-static
a camera move that outlives its scene refuses
a 31s film refuses the app-store-preview slot (G-overrun)
a pose move that outlives its scene refuses
a tween that outlives its scene refuses
a set at or past the scene's end refuses
state writes need a mounted app
a frameless scene needs a document to be the product of
a spotlight without a mounted document refuses
a spotlight that outlives its scene refuses
a morph into the FIRST scene refuses (nothing precedes it)
a morph into a documentless scene refuses
a morph that outlives its scene refuses
a supporting frame names its own document
a supporting frame stays on the stage
a supporting frame supports a primary mount
a supporting frame is sized by a real stage fraction
a supporting frame depth stays in [-1, 1]

pose._note: The device pose track obeys cameraAt's hold-then-move law over six axes, LINEAR pins exact by hand. Home is the zero pose. Move 1: at 100ms for 400ms to turn 20, tilt -8, roll 0, x 0.1, y -0.05, scale 0.9. Move 2: at 800ms for 200ms back to zero/1.

cases.name: before the first move: home
halfway through move 1: exact midpoints on every axis
held between moves
halfway back: the move starts FROM the held pose

float._note: floatAt is a pure function of time: y = 0.004 sin(2 pi t/5.3), turn = 1.6 sin(2 pi t/7.1), tilt = 0.9 sin(2 pi t/6.2 + 1). Pinned at t=0 and at each track's quarter period, where the sine is exactly 0 or 1. Tolerance 1e-9.

cases.name: a quarter of the y period: y at its full amplitude
a quarter of the turn period: turn at its full amplitude
half the y period: y back through zero

cut._note: The CUT LAW: cut lives on the INCOMING scene and owns BOTH edges of its boundary - its own enter fade and the outgoing scene's leave fade - so one word cuts the whole edit. With scene 1 set to cut=hard, the scene 0 -> 1 boundary is a hard cut in both directions while the scene 1 -> 2 boundary stays a fade (scene 2 is fade). Alpha values are exact hand arithmetic against SCENE_FADE_MS=320.

cases.name: the outgoing scene does NOT fade out into a hard cut (would be 0.5 under fade)
a hard-cut scene does NOT fade in (would be 0.5 under fade)
the hard scene still fades OUT into a fade successor
the fade successor still fades IN

writes._note: State-write sampling at frameMs=100 (10fps keeps every number exact hand arithmetic). Scene 1 (starts 2000ms) gains one set (locked=true at local 200ms) and two LINEAR tweens over local 500..1500ms: calories 0->101 rounded, ratio 0->1 unrounded. A set is attributed to exactly one frame like a tap. A tween emits every frame while live, and the frame at/past its end emits the EXACT to (never the eased approximation) exactly once - the frame after that emits nothing, because the store already holds it.

cases.name: the frame before the set carries nothing
the set's frame carries it once
the tweens' first frame emits their from values
40% through: round bites the counter, not the ratio (40.4 -> 40)
the end frame emits the exact to, once
the frame after the end writes nothing

focus._note: The SPOTLIGHT window follows the caption envelope exactly (easeOut 300ms in, linear 240ms out, min of both), so the two chrome layers breathe identically. Scene 1 (starts 2000ms, 3000ms long) gains one focus row at local 500ms for 2000ms on #btn. Pins avoid the eased mid-curve (Conformance/motion's law): fully entered at/after 300ms into the window, the linear out ramp at exact arithmetic, outside the window null.

cases.name: before the window there is no spotlight
fully entered 300ms into the window
the linear out ramp: 120ms before the end is half gone
at the window's end the spotlight is gone

morph._note: The HERO transition runs from the scene's first instant for forMs, LINEAR pins exact. Scene 1 gains morph {#btn, 1000ms}. p is the eased progress; after forMs the morph is null - the component has landed and the scene owns it. A MORPH IMPLIES THE HARD BOUNDARY: the hero transition is the edit, so with scene 1 keeping cut=fade the enter edge and the predecessor's leave edge both hold alpha 1 - a crossfade veil over the flight would dim the very layers the morph exists to show.

cases.name: the boundary instant is progress zero
halfway: exact linear midpoint
at forMs the morph is over
the predecessor does not fade out into a morph (would be 0.5 under fade)
a morph scene does not fade in even with cut=fade (would be 0.5)
